name: Dielectric Phase Inversion Glove DPIG-4 'Secondskin'
description:
The Dielectric Phase Inversion Glove is a full-hand wearable weapons platform that generates a controlled dielectric phase inversion field across the glove's outer surface, activated through a pressure-sensitive grip trigger integrated into the palm. On contact with a target, the field inverts the dielectric properties of whatever material it touches — organic tissue, polymer armor, composite materials — causing a rapid destabilization of molecular bonding at the contact interface. Against unprotected flesh, this manifests as a severe disruption of nerve conduction and localized cellular delamination; the sensation is described by those who survive brief contact as 'my hand stopped being my hand.' Against armored surfaces, the inversion causes surface-layer spalling and micro-fracturing that degrades protective integrity over repeated contacts.

ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC developed the DPIG-4 as part of their covert operations wearables line, specifically addressing the need for a weapon with zero ballistic signature — no projectile, no beam, no audible discharge. In a world saturated with acoustic and optical sensors, a weapon that kills through a handshake is functionally invisible to most surveillance architectures. The glove itself is visually indistinguishable from premium smart-fabric work gloves at a casual inspection; the activation hardware is embedded in the lining, and the power cell is housed in a slim cuff that passes as a fashion accessory.

The DPIG-4's weakness is its requirement for physical contact, which demands that operators be trained in close-contact engagement. ZHENG-DAO sells it exclusively through channels that require the purchaser to demonstrate certified hand-to-hand combat proficiency — a requirement that is circumvented regularly on the black market. The weapon has a disquieting cultural resonance: in Meridian 88, where business deals, social hierarchies, and criminal agreements are all sealed with physical contact, the idea that a handshake could be a lethal act has entered the city's social paranoia.
tier_availability: Black market; official sales restricted to ZHENG-DAO approved contractors
legality: Prohibited — classified as an assassination device under Meridian 88 Covert Weapons Statute 7
specifications:
activation method: Palm pressure trigger — 0.3 kg activation threshold
field duration: Continuous while grip engaged
power source: ZHENG-DAO FlexCell cuff battery — 40 minutes continuous use
field intensity: Adjustable via thumb-dial: suppression / incapacitation / lethal
weight: 180 grams (glove and cuff combined)
detection: Passes standard metal detection; fails advanced bioelectric scanners
recharge time: 22 minutes via standard port
tactical_use: Deployed almost exclusively in close-access covert operations: assassinations designed to appear natural, interrogations in monitored environments, and bodyguard-penetration scenarios. Operators are trained to use the suppression setting for control and compliance, escalating only when lethal authorization is confirmed. The glove's invisibility to standard security scans makes it the preferred weapon for operations inside secure facilities where ballistic weapons cannot be brought in. Some operators wear two — one set to suppression, one to lethal — on opposite hands.
cultural_context: The Secondskin has seeded a specific social anxiety in Meridian 88's business and criminal elite: contact paranoia. High-value individuals have begun refusing handshakes, insisting on observed physical greetings, or wearing their own bioelectric detection rings. The phenomenon has been covered in lifestyle media as a quirky security trend, but its roots are in genuine documented cases of DPIG-4 assassinations. Ironically, ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC's own executive staff are rumored to wear detection hardware at all public appearances.
known_users: At least one documented use by a sitting mid-tier corporate executive (case sealed)
story_hooks: A prominent criminal arbitrator dies of apparent cardiac arrest during a deal. The coroner finds nothing — but a street-level fixer notices the arbitrator's hand has a faint cellular delamination pattern that matches DPIG-4 contact. Someone at that table was wearing one.

A DPIG-4 surfaces with its intensity dial removed and replaced with a fixed lethal-only circuit. The modification is clean and professional. ZHENG-DAO wants to know who performed it — because it wasn't one of their engineers.

A new bioelectric detection ring is flooding the market, supposedly able to identify an active DPIG-4 within arm's reach. The rings are real — but they're manufactured by ZHENG-DAO under a shell brand. The company is selling the antidote to its own poison.
An operator is hired to retrieve a DPIG-4 from a target who doesn't know they have it — it was planted in their belongings to frame them for a killing that hasn't happened yet.
